Nothing is wrong with your invocation—the final line confirms Jenkins started successfully.

The launcher polls `/login` while Jenkins boots. Its first retry hit a closed port, then Jenkins’ HTTP server came up but still returned 503 during initialization; a later retry succeeded. The script currently exposes those expected transient `curl` diagnostics because it uses `--show-error`.


```sh

```

content.text:
No. `scan` sends Jenkins an immediate multibranch-index request. Jenkins then contacts GitHub, discovers the configured `main` branch and eligible pull requests, and creates or updates their Jenkins child jobs.

The CLI only prints that the scan was requested; it does not display discovered branches.

So “Fetch candidate branches” is understandable but slightly imprecise—it fetches/discovers branches for Jenkins, rather than listing them.
Do build/test jobs start immediately after "scan", or does one still need to do "run"?

A scan can start builds automatically for newly discovered or changed eligible pull requests, depending on the multibranch job’s branch-source triggers.

`run` is still needed when you want an explicit, parameterized comparison—for example, a specific PR, branch, or commit versus a selected baseline—through the trusted `main` child job. It also lets you use `--follow`.

A scan itself does not queue that explicit candidate/baseline comparison.

Could we have scan also print out which branches/PRs it found and is scheduling to run? i.e. print something like what is printed by "run":

Found PR <pr_number> for branch <branch_name>
Queued gkeyll-ci-stellar_cpu as queue item 56
Queue URL: http://127.0.0.1:8080/queue/item/56/

I’ll map the existing `scan` implementation and Jenkins job types first. The example names the Stellar job, but today only the team multibranch client supports `scan`; that distinction determines whether this is a reporting enhancement or a broader CI-design change.

content.text:
<proposed_plan>
# Report multibranch scan discoveries

## Summary

Enhance only `team scan`. It will wait for the requested Jenkins multibranch indexing operation, then report discovered `main` and eligible PR child jobs plus builds Jenkins newly queued or started because of that scan. Stellar, Perlmutter, and personal remain explicit-`run` workflows.

## Implementation Changes

- Capture a pre-scan snapshot of team child jobs and their build queue IDs.
- Request multibranch indexing, retain its queue location, and poll the root job’s indexing computation until completion (maximum five minutes).
- Fetch the post-scan child-job/build state and diff it against the pre-scan snapshot.
- Print:
  - `Found main (Jenkins job main)`
  - `Found PR #<number> (Jenkins job PR-<number>)`
  - one `Queued … as queue item …` plus queue URL line for every new build caused by this scan, including builds that began before reporting.
- Print an explicit “no builds scheduled” result when discovery created or updated no builds.
- On indexing failure or timeout, return nonzero with the multibranch job URL and retain any discovery/build information already available.
- Update team CLI help and documentation to describe scan as discovering configured branches/PRs and reporting Jenkins scheduling decisions.

## Test Plan

- Add mocked Jenkins API tests covering successful discovery with a new PR build, discovery with no new build, queue-to-build transition before reporting, and indexing failure/timeout.
- Verify the scan output includes only `main` and PR child jobs targeting `main`, preserves queue URLs, and does not require a GitHub token.
- Run shell syntax checks and the focused CLI test suite.

## Assumptions

- PR identity is reported as PR number plus Jenkins child-job name; source branch names are not fetched.
- `scan` blocks quietly until indexing completes, up to five minutes.
- Jenkins multibranch indexing uses the root folder computation API, consistent with the [Folders Plugin API](https://javadoc.jenkins.io/plugin/cloudbees-folder/com/cloudbees/hudson/plugins/folder/computed/ComputedFolder.html); its normal role is branch/PR discovery as documented for [Multibranch Pipeline](https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/multibranch/).
</proposed_plan>
Implement the plan.

I’m implementing this as a team-only enhancement: it will snapshot branch jobs/build queue IDs, request indexing, wait for that computation, then report the discovered `main`/PR jobs and builds newly scheduled by the scan.

`team scan` now:

- Snapshots eligible `main`/`PR-<n>` child jobs and build queue IDs.
- Starts multibranch indexing and waits up to five minutes.
- Reports discovered `main` and PR jobs.
- Reports newly queued builds with their Jenkins queue URLs.
- Gives specific errors for rejected, failed, or timed-out scans.

Updated the dispatcher help and team CI README to match.

Verified Bash syntax, help output, diff whitespace, mocked Jenkins API parsing/reporting, and scan completion/failure handling. I did not run against a live Jenkins controller.
In -h for CLI scripts, please list "scan" before "start"
I’ll adjust the shared dispatcher help; it is the only CLI help that presents both `scan` and `start` together.
